demand_analysis.distribution_type: Right-skewed continuous (approximate Normal with outlier influence)

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Slight increase from SAP 3.3 days to recommended 3.33 days

narrative: Material PL1__M98C617E exhibits smooth, high-volume demand averaging 134,175 units per working day with moderate variability (CV=0.63) and 95.4% non-zero demand days. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.79, mean=1.76 days), contributing 39.1% of total demand-during-lead-time variance. The current SAP policy of ordering at MOQ=24,370 units with zero safety stock generates approximately 1,018 orders/year and leaves the material chronically exposed to stockout risk. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 445,299 units and safety stock of 290,933 units reduces total annual cost by 82% to $18,408/year while achieving the 95% service level target.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock is 0 — material is fully exposed to stockout risk under current policy
Lead time CV=0.79 classified as Volatile — supply reliability improvement recommended
3 demand outliers winsorised at 99th percentile (307,275 units)

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth daily demand with high volume and volatile lead times makes continuous review superior to periodic review. The EOQ formula minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Demand variability is the dominant variance driver (60.9%). Safety stock sensitivity to demand forecast accuracy is high — a 10% reduction in demand std would reduce safety stock by ~18,000 units. Lead time volatility (CV=0.79) also warrants supplier performance management.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (24,370) + safety_stock (290,933) = 315,303 is well below max_storage_units (1,025,865). No infeasibility.
